answer:
Run the eval with the `-j 1` option:

```bash
promptfoo eval -j 1
```

The docs say, "By default, promptfoo evaluates all providers concurrently for each prompt. However, you can run evals serially using the `-j 1` option" [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]. They also say this "serializes the eval's **target** calls: one provider and prompt at a time" [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md].

Two caveats from the same page:

- Test cases marked `options.runSerially` run as a separate group before the rest, so the order isn't strictly sequential even at `-j 1`. The docs say "a config using that option does not execute in strict test-case order even at `-j 1`" [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md].
- Model-graded assertions use a different path. If grading grouping is turned off, up to three grader calls can still overlap within a test case. The docs say "up to `PROMPTFOO_ASSERTIONS_MAX_CONCURRENCY` grader calls (3 by default) can still overlap within a single test case" [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md].
